title: Native visit ordering compares raw ISO strings, so offset-formatted seed visits and Z-formatted user visits misorder; Summary can show the wrong next visit
trigger: With the bundled demo loaded (seed visit 'demo-visit-primary-20260915' stored as '2026-09-15T09:00:00-05:00' = 14:00Z, apps/ios/Reva/Resources/seed.json:286), add a visit via VisitEditorView for 2026-09-15 08:00 America/Chicago (stored by RevaDate.iso as '2026-09-15T13:00:00Z', VisitEditorView.swift:109, Models.swift:217). Open Summary and the Visits tab.
expected: Visits ordered by instant: the 08:00 visit (13:00Z) precedes the 09:00 seed visit (14:00Z); Summary 'Your next visit' shows the 08:00 visit.
actual: AppStore.visits sorts with `$0.date < $1.date` on the raw strings. '2026-09-15T09:00:00-05:00' < '2026-09-15T13:00:00Z' lexicographically, so the later seed visit sorts first; SummaryView.nextVisit (SummaryView.swift:20) picks the first upcoming visit in that order and VisitsView (VisitsView.swift:17-19,34) lists them in that order. The same mismatch occurs for any two visits whose instants fall within the offset window (up to ~5 h for -05:00) around a day boundary, and for browser-created visits pulled from the server (Z format) against untouched seed visits.
impact: Wrong 'next visit' on the home screen and wrong Upcoming/Past ordering whenever visit dates mix time-zone offset and Z formats. The records sort (AppStore.swift:90-96) already parses dates, so this is an inconsistency inside one file. ReportEngine.signature and RevaDate.display parse correctly, so no report/staleness corruption; ordering only.
evidence: Source: AppStore.swift:98 string sort; seed.json:286,306,326 use '-05:00' offsets; VisitEditorView.swift:109 writes RevaDate.iso(date); Models.swift:217 ISO8601DateFormatter().string(from:) emits 'Z' UTC. Refutation attempt: checked whether AppStore.init or AppSnapshot.validate normalizes visit dates on load (they do not; AppStore.swift:54-87, Models.swift:169-186) and whether the editor rewrites untouched seed visits (only when a seed visit is edited and saved). Browser parity: apps/web/src/features/visits/VisitsPage.tsx:28-35 sorts by parsed epoch, so the browser orders the same data correctly. Runtime unverified (no simulator permitted); a pure-Swift string-comparison demonstration is requested as ER-04-03.
smallestFix: Sort by `RevaDate.parse($0.date) < RevaDate.parse($1.date)` (tie-break on id), matching the records sort in the same file; optionally normalize visit.date to RevaDate.iso on load or in the seed.
regressionCheck: Unit test in RevaCoreTests (or a new AppStore test target) constructing visits with '2026-09-15T09:00:00-05:00' and '2026-09-15T13:00:00Z' and asserting the Z visit sorts first; snapshot-level check that Summary next visit equals min-by-instant upcoming visit.
ownerTrack: Captain (shared core AppStore.swift); Person 2 for the visit-facing verification

title: Global error alert lives on RootView beneath modal sheets; failures raised while Settings or an editor sheet is open may never be shown
trigger: Open Medical profile > Settings (a .sheet, MedicalProfileView.swift:86), enter an unreachable Server URL (e.g. a closed loopback port) and tap 'Check available services' (SettingsView.swift:27) or 'Check connection'/'Push local snapshot' (SettingsView.swift:56-67). Equivalent paths: any failing store.perform save inside RecordEditorView.swift:75, VisitEditorView.swift:117, MedicalProfileEditor.swift:117, ReportEditorView.swift:40, AddRecordView.swift:265-281 (all presented as sheets).
expected: The error is presented to the user while the sheet is still open, or inline in the sheet, and the sheet stays open so they can correct the input.
actual: checkProviders (AppStore+Providers.swift:32) and sync (AppStore+Sync.swift:132) write store.errorMessage; the only presenter is the `.alert` attached to RootView's Group (RootView.swift:50-58), which sits under the presented sheet. SwiftUI presents that alert from the root hosting controller, which is already presenting the sheet; in that configuration the alert is commonly not shown (UIKit 'already presenting' refusal) until the sheet is dismissed, if at all. For 'Check available services' nothing else changes on screen (providerStatus stays nil = 'Not configured'), so the user sees the progress indicator vanish with no explanation. SymptomEntryEditorView avoids this by rendering its own inline error (SymptomEntryEditorView.swift:105-110,138), which indicates the pattern is known but not applied to the other sheets.
impact: Silent failures on the Settings connection/provider path and on rare save failures in five editor sheets. Data is not lost (saves fail atomically), but the user gets no feedback and may retry blindly or assume success.
evidence: Source proof of modifier placement: RootView.swift:50-58 (alert on root), MedicalProfileView.swift:86 (Settings sheet), SettingsView.swift:27,56-67 (actions), AppStore+Providers.swift:29-33 and AppStore+Sync.swift:130-134 (errorMessage writers), SymptomEntryEditorView.swift:105-110,133-139 (inline pattern). Features/Visits/RecordingSessionView.swift:55 (outside this track) writes store.errorMessage from a sheet too. Refutation attempt: looked for any per-sheet alert modifier or an overlay-window presenter in Features/** (none found by grep for '.alert(' outside RootView). The claim that the underlying alert does not surface is SwiftUI runtime behavior and could not be exercised here (no simulator permitted) — hence candidate, medium confidence; ER-04-02 requests the check.
smallestFix: Attach the same errorMessage-bound `.alert` inside each sheet's NavigationStack content (or render inline errors as SymptomEntryEditorView does); for Settings, also surface provider/connection failures inline via serverStatus/providerStatus text.
regressionCheck: XCUITest: open Settings, set an unreachable URL, tap 'Check available services', assert an alert or inline error appears while the Settings sheet is still presented; repeat for a forced save failure in RecordEditorView (e.g., a repository stub that throws).
ownerTrack: Captain (shared RootView/error boundary); Person 1 for Records/Profile sheets; Person 2 for Visit/Report sheets

title: Visit editor time-zone picker shifts the already-entered wall-clock time, defaults to America/Chicago regardless of device zone, and offers only six zones; browser keeps wall-clock time and includes the device zone
trigger: On a device in America/New_York, open Add visit, set 'Date & time' to 10:00 (displayed in the default America/Chicago zone, VisitEditorView.swift:21,43-44), then change 'Time zone' to America/New_York and save.
expected: The appointment is 10:00 in the clinic's zone (New York), i.e. the entered wall-clock time is kept when the zone changes — which is what the browser editor does (apps/web/src/features/visits/VisitEditor.tsx:20,55-56 with visitDates.ts:31-44), and the default zone is the device zone.
actual: The DatePicker binds a Date instant (@State date) and the zone only changes the picker's display environment (VisitEditorView.swift:43-44); switching zones re-displays the same instant as 11:00 New York. If the user does not notice the shift, the saved visit (VisitEditorView.swift:109-110) is one hour off. The zone list is a fixed six-entry array (VisitEditorView.swift:47-50) with no device-zone entry; the default is the string 'America/Chicago' (line 21).
impact: Secondary-path appointment time errors for users outside the six listed zones or who set the time before the zone; native/browser behavior differs for the same action. DST arithmetic itself is correct (instant-based; display via RevaDate.display in the visit zone everywhere).
evidence: VisitEditorView.swift:20-21,43-52,99-117; Models.swift:217; browser VisitEditor.tsx:20,48-56 and visitDates.ts:16-44 (wall-clock components stored as a string until save). Refutation attempt: verified that no onChange(of: zone) handler re-derives the Date to preserve wall-clock components (none present) and that the default zone is not derived from TimeZone.current (it is a literal).
smallestFix: On zone change, re-derive `date` so the calendar components stay constant in the new zone (as visitDates.ts does); default `zone` to TimeZone.current.identifier and include it in the Picker list (mirroring VisitEditor.tsx:125).
regressionCheck: Unit test on the conversion helper: entering 10:00 in Chicago then switching to New_York yields an instant displaying 10:00 New_York; UI test that the picker's displayed time is unchanged after a zone switch.

title: 'Create pre-visit brief' silently does nothing while a Gemini summary is in flight (connected AI on)
trigger: Turn on 'Use connected AI', save a document or symptom entry (AddRecordView.swift:277-279 / SymptomEntryEditorView.swift:136 start summarizeWithAI in the background, setting isProviderBusy), immediately open a visit and tap 'Create pre-visit brief'.
expected: Either the button is disabled while the provider is busy, or the tap yields a visible message ('A connected request is still running').
actual: The button is disabled only by the local `generating` flag (VisitDetailView.swift:76). prepare() (lines 165-171) calls generatePreferredReport, which returns false without setting errorMessage or notice when isProviderBusy is true (AppStore+AI.swift:36). The button shows a spinner for one run-loop turn and reverts; nothing else happens.
impact: Confusing no-op on the visit preparation path when connected AI is enabled; the user may assume preparation is broken. Local (non-AI) path is unaffected. ReportView already guards its Regenerate button with store.isProviderBusy (ReportView.swift:76-79), so the omission is specific to VisitDetailView.
evidence: VisitDetailView.swift:68-76,165-171; AppStore+AI.swift:34-38 (silent `return false`); comparison ReportView.swift:76-79. Refutation attempt: checked whether perform()/notice is set on the busy branch (it is not) and whether any other UI disables the button on isProviderBusy (none).
smallestFix: Add `|| store.isProviderBusy` to the button's .disabled and show the same 'Working with connected service…' label ReportView uses; or set `notice` in the busy branch of generatePreferredReport.
regressionCheck: Unit test on AppStore with isProviderBusy = true and useConnectedAI = true: generatePreferredReport returns false AND leaves a non-nil notice/errorMessage; UI test that the button is disabled while busy.

title: Visit and record editors save a full copy captured at open time, so an AI result that lands while the editor is open (report or summary) is silently reverted on Save
trigger: Connected AI on. On VisitDetailView tap 'Create pre-visit brief' (async), then tap the toolbar 'Edit' (VisitDetailView.swift:161, still enabled while generating), change only the title, wait for the AI brief to save (AppStore+AI.swift:80-81), then tap Save in the editor. Record analogue: AddRecordView saves with AI on (summarizeWithAI starts), open the record, tap 'Edit record & review text', add a note, wait for the AI summary to land (AppStore+AI.swift:26-28), Save.
expected: Editing unrelated fields (title/provider/clinic or record notes) keeps the freshly generated report / AI summary, as ReportEditorView already does by rebasing on store.visit (ReportEditorView.swift:37).
actual: VisitEditorView.save() starts from `existing` captured when the sheet opened (VisitEditorView.swift:100-104) and writes it back whole, including `report == nil`, so the AI brief that was saved meanwhile is discarded and VisitDetailView returns to 'Create pre-visit brief' (and the pushed ReportView shows 'No brief yet'). RecordEditorView.save() writes its @State copy of the record (RecordEditorView.swift:61-75), so `summary`/`summaryModel` revert to the pre-AI local excerpt even when the text was not changed, and the version bumps because summary differs (AppStore+Records.swift:20-24).
impact: Loss of an AI result the user paid for and must regenerate; only reachable with connected AI on and an editor opened during the in-flight request (a window of seconds). Local-only flows are synchronous and not affected. This is the 'newer edit overwrites delayed AI' direction; the protected direction (delayed AI overwriting newer edits) is correctly guarded in AppStore+AI.swift:17-22,51-56.
evidence: VisitEditorView.swift:99-117; RecordEditorView.swift:15-22,61-75; AppStore+AI.swift:17-28,74-81; ReportEditorView.swift:37 (correct rebasing pattern). Refutation attempt: confirmed no `store.visit(existing.id)`/`store.record(original.id)` rebase in either save(), and that AppStore.save(visit)/save(record) replace the whole element (AppStore+Visits.swift:16-20, AppStore+Records.swift:25).
smallestFix: In both save() functions, start from the store's latest element (`store.visit(existing.id) ?? existing`, `store.record(original.id) ?? original`) and apply only the fields the editor owns; optionally disable 'Edit' while `generating`.
regressionCheck: AppStore-level test: save a visit with a report while an editor draft based on the report-less copy exists, then apply the editor's field changes through the rebased path and assert `report != nil`; same for record summaryModel.

title: Camera-scanned documents are saved as kind 'Notes', so the 'Scan' filter misses them; record kind is never user-editable
trigger: On a physical iPhone, Add record > 'Scan a document', capture pages, review, Save to Records. Then in Records choose the 'Scan' filter.
expected: A document produced by 'Scan a document' appears under 'Scan' (the intake row and the filter chip use the same word), or the kind can be corrected in the editor.
actual: DocumentScanner pages are rendered into a PDF (AddRecordView.swift:139-165) and ingested as mimeType 'application/pdf' (DocumentImportService.swift:288). AddRecordView assigns `kind: item.mimeType.hasPrefix("image") ? "Scan" : "Notes"` (line 268), so camera scans become 'Notes' with the generic doc.text symbol (Models.swift:47-57). Only photo-library images become 'Scan'. RecordEditorView has no kind field (RecordEditorView.swift:28-49), and 'Labs'/'Imaging'/'Procedure' kinds exist only in seed data.
impact: Filter incoherence for the most likely real-world intake path (camera); users cannot categorize their own uploads. Data is intact (originals, page mapping and OCR warnings are preserved), so this is a secondary-path categorization defect.
evidence: AddRecordView.swift:139-165,268; DocumentImportService.swift:288; RecordsView.swift:18-20 (filter list) and 22-28 (kind equality); RecordEditorView.swift:28-49; Models.swift:47-57. Refutation attempt: checked whether ImportedDocument carries a scan flag or whether AddRecordView tracks the scanner origin to set the kind (neither exists).
smallestFix: Track intake origin in AddRecordView (a `scanned` flag set in the scanner onFinish path) and use it for the kind; add a kind Picker (Notes/Labs/Imaging/Procedure/Scan) to AddRecordView's review card and RecordEditorView.
regressionCheck: Unit-level: a scanner-origin ImportedDocument saved through the intake path yields kind == 'Scan'; UI: after a camera scan the 'Scan' filter lists the record.

title: ReportView question numbers use accent (heart red) on petal for 12pt bold caption text: 4.45:1, below the theme's own AA guidance
trigger: Open any visit brief with questions.
expected: Small red text on petal uses RevaTheme.accentText (deep red, 6.8:1) as Theme.swift prescribes.
actual: ReportView.swift:55-56 renders `Text("\(index + 1)").font(.caption.bold()).foregroundStyle(RevaTheme.accent)` on `RevaTheme.soft`. Theme.swift:21-22 documents that accent alone is 4.45:1 on petal and reserves accentText for chip labels and small red text. Recomputed WCAG relative luminance: #B84250 L=0.147, #FAE6E5 L=0.826 -> 4.45:1 (< 4.5:1 for non-large text; 12pt bold is not 'large').
impact: Marginal AA contrast failure on one small element; every other text pairing checked in Features/** uses accentText/primary/secondary on soft or accent on white/canvas (>= 5.0:1).
evidence: ReportView.swift:53-58; Theme.swift:17-25; design/palette.json accent.contrast and accentText.contrast values (4.45 not listed, computed). Refutation attempt: checked whether the number is decorative (accessibilityHidden) — it is not; VoiceOver reads it as part of the row.
smallestFix: Change the foregroundStyle on ReportView.swift:55 to RevaTheme.accentText.
regressionCheck: Grep Features/** for `foregroundStyle(RevaTheme.accent)` combined with `.background(RevaTheme.soft` on Text and assert none; optional contrast script (ER-04-05).
ownerTrack: Person 2 (report view); Captain for theme guidance

title: Exported visit-brief PDF still uses the superseded teal (#0A5B6C) for title, headings and header instead of the heart palette
trigger: ReportView > 'Share visit brief' on a fresh brief.
expected: Export chrome follows the current heart-red/ivory palette (or a documented print-neutral variant).
actual: ReportPDFRenderer.swift:208-210 defines `teal = UIColor(red: 10/255, green: 91/255, blue: 108/255)` and applies it at lines 126, 133, 141, 181; the variable name and value belong to the palette that design/palette.json marks as superseded.
impact: Style only; content, citations, pagination logic and staleness gating are unaffected. Note: this file is outside Track 04's assigned scope paths (Device/); recorded here because E05/K01 cover the export, flagged for de-duplication with the Device/native-core track.
evidence: ReportPDFRenderer.swift:126,133,141,181,208-210; design/palette.json 'supersedes' note; Theme.swift:13-15 current values. Refutation attempt: searched for a palette import in the renderer (none; UIKit colors are literal).
smallestFix: Replace `teal` with UIColor(hex: 0x8C2F3B) (deepRed for print legibility) via the existing UIColor(hex:) initializer in Theme.swift:30-36, and rename the property.
regressionCheck: Grep Device/** for 'teal' returns nothing; visual check of an exported PDF.

title: Accessibility robustness: fixed-size badges with scaled text, fixed point sizes on Welcome, a 17pt dismiss target, notices/inline errors not announced, unused symptom auto-focus, decorative chevrons/share icon without explicit labels
trigger: Run with Larger Accessibility Sizes (AX3-AX5) and VoiceOver on Summary, Medical profile, a visit brief and the symptom editor.
expected: Text scales without clipping; controls have >= 44pt targets; status/error text is announced; decorative icons are hidden from VoiceOver; intended auto-focus works.
actual: (a) SummaryView.swift:137-139 initials in a fixed 36x36 frame with scaled caption text; MedicalProfileView.swift:26-29 initials in a fixed 60x60 frame with title2; ReportView.swift:55-56 question numbers in a fixed 24x24 circle; ViewComponents.swift:79 IconTile 42x42 with title3 symbol — at AX sizes text/symbols exceed the frames. (b) WelcomeView.swift:18,20 use fixed .system(size: 64/48) which do not scale with Dynamic Type. (c) SummaryView.swift:34-38 dismiss control is a bare 17pt symbol with no minimum frame. (d) SummaryView.swift:30-40 notice banner and SymptomEntryEditorView.swift:105-110 inline error are plain Text with no announcement or status trait. (e) SymptomEntryEditorView.swift:20,48 declares @FocusState symptomFocused and binds it but never sets it, so the intended auto-focus does not happen. (f) RecordRow.swift:28-29, VisitRow.swift:22 chevrons and SourcePreview.swift:32 image-only ShareLink label carry no explicit accessibility label/hidden trait. Positive: filter chips set .isSelected (RecordsView.swift:53), image-only toolbar buttons are labeled (RecordsView.swift:84, VisitsView.swift:57, MedicalProfileView.swift:83, SummaryView.swift:38,140), IconTile is accessibilityHidden, symptom fields carry labels.
impact: Cosmetic clipping and weaker screen-reader feedback at accessibility sizes; no functional block. Runtime unverified (no simulator permitted).
evidence: Line citations above, each verified with sed. Refutation attempt: checked for @ScaledMetric or minimumScaleFactor on the fixed frames (none) and for UIAccessibility.post/accessibilityAddTraits(.updatesFrequently) on notices (none).
smallestFix: Use @ScaledMetric for the badge frames or drop fixed sizes; replace fixed .system(size:) with text styles; give the dismiss button .frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44); post UIAccessibility.announcement (or .accessibilityAddTraits(.updatesFrequently)) when notice/saveError change; set symptomFocused = true onAppear; add .accessibilityHidden(true) to chevrons and .accessibilityLabel("Share") to the ShareLink.
regressionCheck: Accessibility Inspector audit on Summary/Profile/Brief at AX5; VoiceOver pass confirming notice announcements.

title: Unsaved-changes protection exists only in the symptom editor; the visit, record, profile, report-notes and import-review sheets discard edits on Cancel or swipe-down without confirmation
trigger: Type into any of: VisitEditorView, RecordEditorView, MedicalProfileEditor, ReportEditorView, or the AddRecordView review card (after extraction), then tap Cancel or swipe the sheet down.
expected: Consistent behavior across editors: confirm before discarding non-trivial edits and block interactive dismissal while dirty (as SymptomEntryEditorView.swift:117,121-128 does).
actual: VisitEditorView.swift:80, RecordEditorView.swift:52, MedicalProfileEditor.swift:98, ReportEditorView.swift:34 and AddRecordView.swift:119 call dismiss() directly and do not set interactiveDismissDisabled. No persistence happens (no ghost records), so this is a lost-edit UX inconsistency, not data corruption.
impact: Accidental loss of in-progress corrections (notably reviewed OCR text in AddRecordView, which is the longest to redo).
evidence: Line citations above; positive pattern in SymptomEntryEditorView.swift:115-128. Refutation attempt: confirmed no .interactiveDismissDisabled or confirmationDialog in the five views.
smallestFix: Reuse the symptom editor's hasChanges/confirmDiscard/interactiveDismissDisabled pattern in the other editors (a small shared modifier would suffice).
regressionCheck: UI test: edit a field, swipe down, assert the sheet remains and a discard dialog appears.

title: Past visits list oldest-first on native (browser lists past visits newest-first); native 'Upcoming' relies on status only while the browser also uses the date
trigger: Visits tab > Past with several completed visits; or leave an 'upcoming' visit un-marked after its date passes.
expected: Past visits newest-first (most recent memory on top), matching the browser (VisitsPage.tsx:28-35); an overdue 'upcoming' visit is surfaced consistently on both platforms.
actual: AppStore.visits is a single ascending sort (AppStore.swift:98) reused by VisitsView.filtered (VisitsView.swift:17-19), so Past shows the oldest visit first. Native filters by status only; the browser moves date-passed visits to Past automatically, so the same snapshot can show a visit under 'Upcoming' natively and 'Past' in the browser.
impact: Ordering/UX parity only; no data effect.
evidence: AppStore.swift:98; VisitsView.swift:17-19,34; browser VisitsPage.tsx:20-35. Refutation attempt: looked for a reversed sort in VisitsView (none).
smallestFix: In VisitsView, reverse the order for the Past segment (or expose upcoming/past projections from AppStore); align the upcoming predicate with the browser's status+date rule or document the difference.
regressionCheck: Unit test on the projection: Past returns descending instants.

title: Visit lifecycle gaps: no way to delete a visit (native or browser) and visit notes are only editable after a brief exists
trigger: Add an appointment by mistake; or try to add personal notes to a visit before generating a brief.
expected: CRUD completeness: a delete action (cascading bookings/recordings to satisfy AppSnapshot.validate) and notes editable from the visit editor.
actual: AppStore+Visits.swift:10-32 offers only save and generateReport; VisitDetailView.swift:146-150 only toggles status. Visit.notes is edited solely through ReportEditorView, reachable from ReportView.swift:63,86 (requires a report). No deleteVisit exists in apps/web/src either (grep), so this is a product gap rather than a parity defect.
impact: A mistaken visit can only be moved to Past; notes cannot be captured pre-brief. No data integrity effect.
evidence: AppStore+Visits.swift:10-32; VisitDetailView.swift:146-150; ReportView.swift:63,86; VisitEditorView.swift:35-77 (no notes field); Models.swift:178-181 (validate requires bookings/recordings to reference existing visits, so deletion must cascade).
smallestFix: Add `deleteVisit(id)` in AppStore+Visits that removes the visit and its bookings/recordings in one mutate, with a confirmation dialog in VisitDetailView; add a 'Your notes' TextEditor to VisitEditorView.
regressionCheck: Unit test: deleting a visit with a booking and recording leaves a snapshot that passes validate(); UI test for the confirmation.

title: Profile keeps isDemo=true after the user replaces every demo field, so it stays labeled 'Fictional demo profile'
trigger: Edit medical profile: replace name, DOB, allergies, medications, conditions with real details and save.
expected: Either the label clears once the profile no longer contains demo content, or the UI explains that the label describes the profile's origin.
actual: MedicalProfileEditor.save() copies `profile` (line 109) including isDemo; AppStore+Profile.swift never changes it; MedicalProfileView.swift:32-34 shows 'Fictional demo profile' whenever isDemo is true. The browser has the same semantics (App.tsx:141, MedicalProfilePage.tsx:74), so it is consistent but potentially misleading for a user who has entered real facts.
impact: Labeling clarity only; facts persist correctly and blanks remain 'Not provided'.
evidence: MedicalProfileEditor.swift:108-117; AppStore+Profile.swift:11-35; MedicalProfileView.swift:32-34. Refutation attempt: confirmed no path clears PatientProfile.isDemo in apps/ios (grep).
smallestFix: Clear isDemo when the saved name differs from the seed name and no field still contains '(Synthetic)'/'Fictional', or reword the caption to 'Started from the fictional demo profile'.
regressionCheck: Unit test on saveMedicalProfile with real-looking input asserting isDemo == false (or caption test).

title: AddRecordView: stale import error persists after a successful photo/scan import, and Cancel does not cancel the running extraction Task
trigger: (a) Trigger an import error (e.g., unsupported file), then choose a photo or scan that succeeds. (b) Start a multi-page scanned PDF import and tap Cancel while 'Reading your document' is shown.
expected: (a) The previous error banner clears when a new extraction succeeds. (b) Cancel stops the OCR work (DocumentImportService honors Task cancellation at DocumentImportService.swift:324,331).
actual: (a) Only ingest(url:) resets importError (AddRecordView.swift:216-219); the photo path (127-138) and scanner path (139-173) do not, and the banner is rendered outside the state switch (111-115), so it stays under the successful preview. (b) The Tasks created at lines 123, 128, 143, 182, 190, 196 are not stored; Cancel (line 119) dismisses the sheet while extraction continues (bounded: 30 pages, 10 OCR pages, 2600px edge) and setImported later writes to a dismissed view.
impact: Minor confusion and wasted bounded CPU; no persistence occurs before review, so no ghost records or lost originals.
evidence: AddRecordView.swift:111-115,119,123,128,127-138,139-173,182,190,196,216-223; DocumentImportService.swift:324,331. Refutation attempt: verified there is no @State Task handle or onDisappear cancellation in AddRecordView.
smallestFix: Reset importError at the start of every extraction path (move the reset into setImported/working=true), keep the extraction Task in @State and cancel it in Cancel/onDisappear.
regressionCheck: UI test: error then successful photo import shows no banner; unit test that cancelling the task makes ingest throw CancellationError promptly.
